title: What Actually Is Docker?
sources: Docker, 'What is a Container?' (docker.com/resources/what-container): a container packages up code and all its dependencies so the application runs quickly and reliably from one computing environment to another; containers share the machine's OS kernel and don't need a full OS per app, unlike virtual machines
Wikipedia, 'Docker (software)': released as open source in March 2013; containers run on a shared host kernel and are more lightweight than virtual machines
Merriam-Webster / Cambridge Dictionary, 'docker': a person who loads and unloads ships at a port (a dock worker / longshoreman)
Docker Docs, 'Docker overview': containers are lightweight and contain everything needed to run the application, so you don't need to rely on what's installed on the host

lines.text: You know when an app works on your laptop,
but crashes on your friend's computer?
That's because it's missing something, like the right version.
Docker fixes that by packing your app
and everything it needs into one little box,
Now that box runs exactly the same
on your laptop, a server, or the cloud.
it doesn't drag along a whole operating system,
And the name? A docker is a dock worker,
lines.caps: AND THE *NAME? | A *DOCKER | IS A DOCK *WORKER

lines.text: the person who loads shipping containers onto ships.
So next time it works on your machine,
